name: Astatine

discovery.discoverer: Dale R. Corson, Kenneth Ross MacKenzie & Emilio Segrè

occurrence: The rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — at any given moment, only a few grams exist in the entire planet's crust, from uranium/thorium decay chains.
majorUses: Experimental targeted alpha-particle cancer therapy (astatine-211), still in research/clinical trial stages
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive; its extreme rarity and short half-lives mean it's studied only in minute, carefully controlled quantities.
notableCharacteristics: So scarce and short-lived (its most stable isotope has a half-life of just over 8 hours) that no one has ever seen a visible, bulk sample of astatine — its physical appearance is inferred rather than observed.
whyHere: Named from the Greek 'astatos', meaning 'unstable', astatine sits at the bottom of the halogen group where increasing atomic size and radioactivity converge, making it too scarce and short-lived to behave like a normal, isolable halogen.
didYouKnow: Astatine is so rare that scientists estimate less than 30 grams exist naturally on Earth at any given time, spread invisibly thin across the entire planet's crust — nobody has ever actually seen a visible piece of it.
genZNote: So rare literally no human has ever seen a visible chunk of it. The periodic table's most elusive main character.
